subject: Hybrid endpoint TTFT & sustained token-throughput waiver request

Subject: Hybrid endpoint — TTFT and sustained token/sec expectations

Hi Connor / Evelyn,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo — StellarTech's product team is excited about Redwood's hybrid endpoint option. Before we move to a POC, procurement flagged two items we need in writing around SLA commitments for streaming vs non-streaming delivery:

- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): for our UI use-case we need median TTFT <= 300ms for streaming endpoints (interactive chat).
- Sustained throughput: for background batch summarization we expect 45–60 tokens/sec sustained for async endpoints during business hours.

Stellar's compliance folks understand that streaming semantics differ from non-streaming, so they asked whether Redwood can agree to a waiver/carveout for the streaming TTFT vs batch sustained token/sec numbers (i.e., different SLO buckets). If you can provide a short carveout doc and a traffic profile we can run a brief procurement review.

I've attached a traffic sample (small) and procurement's baseline SLA (for context). Can we get a draft carveout and an engineer note on what guarantees are realistic for a mixed model?

Thanks,
Elena Rojas
Director of Product
StellarTech

Subject: RE: Hybrid endpoint — TTFT and sustained token/sec expectations

Elena, Connor —

Thanks — dug into the traffic sample. High level engineering guidance below (we'll attach a formal traffic-readout PDF in the next message):

- Streaming TTFT: median TTFT targets are achievable in the 150–350ms window for compact open models (7–13B) with our prefix caching + continuous batching. For larger families (70B+), expect TTFT to increase; recommend we specify TTFT per model family in the carveout.

- Sustained tokens/sec (async endpoints): 50 tokens/sec sustained is reasonable on a dedicated pool for mid-sized models, assuming concurrency and typical sequence lengths (~256 tokens). If your batch jobs use sequences >1024 tokens, sustained throughput drops ~25–40%.

Proposed carveout approach (technical summary):
1) Split SLOs by delivery mode: streaming TTFT SLO (median) and async sustained token/sec SLO (p95 sustained window).
2) Define model family buckets (small/medium/large) with numeric SLOs for each.
3) Add a clause for cache-warmup window (first 15 minutes of a novel workload may not meet steady-state sustained throughput).
4) Provide a canary/fallback policy: if streaming TTFT > SLO for >5% of requests over a 1 hour window, traffic can be routed to a sync variant with proportional credit/discount (to preserve availability).

I've attached a concise traffic-readout + baseline numbers (traffic_profile.csv) and a draft carveout PDF for legal. Aditya — can you confirm the safe default numbers for the canary trigger and fallback discount (we usually do 10% credit for sustained infra breach while fallback engaged)?

-Karthik

Date: 2027-08-23T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Hybrid endpoint — TTFT and sustained token/sec expectations

Elena / team — quick engineering confirmation on the proposed guardrails:

- Canary trigger: streaming TTFT breach defined as p50 TTFT > agreed SLO for 5%+ of requests within a rolling 1-hour window. That is implementable via our tracing + sampling pipeline; we can surface alerts to both Redwood and Stellar ops.
- Fallback behaviour: automatic route to a compatible sync endpoint when the canary triggers. Sync endpoint will have documented sustained tokens/sec SLO and a tolerance credit applied to invoices while fallback active.
- Warmup: first-connection coldstart variability is real. We'll include a 15-minute warmup exception and explicit cache-warmup measurement hooks to demonstrate steady-state.
- Numbers we recommend for initial contract (subject to model family):
  * Small models (<=13B): streaming TTFT median <= 250ms; async sustained 60 tokens/sec
  * Medium (14–70B): streaming TTFT median <= 350ms; async sustained 45 tokens/sec
  * Large (70B+): streaming TTFT median <= 600ms; async sustained 20–30 tokens/sec

I'll also note operational bullets for the carveout PDF: sample queries we used, expected sequence length assumptions, and how we measure tokens/sec (server-side token emission rates).

-Aditya Rao
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the patience. We've reviewed Karthik and Aditya's technical notes and drafted a short carveout (attached) that:

- Separates SLOs into streaming and async delivery modes, with model-family buckets.
- Explicitly documents warmup exceptions (15 minutes) and the canary/fallback process.
- Includes measurement definitions (p50/p95 TTFT, 1-hour sustained-window for tokens/sec) and a remediation credit schedule tied to duration and impact.

From a contract perspective, two asks from Stellar procurement before we sign:
1) Confirm which model families you'll rely on for the POC (so we pick concrete numbers).
2) Confirm acceptance of the fallback routing + credit approach (procurement wants a clear financial remedy rather than an escalation-only path).

If procurement confirms those two items, we can convert the draft into an addendum for signature (we can use DocuSign and link it to the HubSpot deal).

Best,
